heroHeadline: Trump Signs Space Academy Order in Houston as Judge Rejects Third Bid to Move Hush Money Case to Federal Court
heroSubtitle: President Trump signed an executive order Friday, August 28, 2026 (Day 586) at NASA's Johnson Space Center in Houston establishing the nation's first US Space Academy — chaired by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman with a 120-day mandate on governance, curriculum, and site selection — during a visit that also honored the Artemis II crew with medals. The same day, US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein rejected Trump's third attempt to move his New York hush money conviction to federal court, ruling the grounds for removal were 'neither new nor legally sufficient.' The developments followed Trump's August 26 declaration of a national emergency over foreign-made bulk-power-system equipment citing sabotage and cybersecurity risks, capping a week that saw the Canada trade war escalate and Lake Ontario renamed 'Lake America'; Trump's approval rating held near a second-term low, with the FiftyPlusOne polling average at roughly 36% approve / 59% disapprove as of August 29.
